items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: Condon as a matter of fact is of all the really close friends I've got

ctx.x: Both Bix and McPartland, whom we've mentioned, worked those boats. And apparently so did Brunus on occasion. Now, this may have been their first contact with Brunus. And it would be about 23, 24 in the summers of those years.

They also played at Lake Delavan. In Wisconsin. Well, Condon and McPartland. Oh, yes. And a wonderful amateur. We always thought of him as an amateur, Fritz Nielsen, a pianist. It's probable that Fritz was the best of the Chicago pianists.
Did that be in those years? Yes. Or earliest 20s?

items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: Connon denies that, of course. But I think that's just because Connon doesn't like tags on anything.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, by 28, there was a pretty well-established Chicago style, was there? Uh, anybody from Chicago would be recognized if he strayed, uh, a couple hundred miles away.

Connon denies that, of course. But I think that's just because Connon doesn't like tags on anything. Uh. Uh, to me there always has been. I think it's as definable as, let's say, Kansas City, certainly.
If not. Uh, still, there was a little crossing here. For example, Wingy's bands might be called Chicago bands. And with Wingy leading them, they were New Orleans bands.
